title: Render Manifest
description: The authoritative contract for the Stage 1 -> Stage 2 boundary. Stage 1 (src/passport_generator.py) is the provider; the render engines behind src/render_stage.py are the consumers. A manifest carries the DECISIONS made about a SKU (which template, what size the carton is, what goes on the label) rather than the raw passport, so a renderer never has to re-derive routing or dimensions and never has to import Stage 1 internals. Plain JSON Schema is the chosen artifact because assets/blender/render_driver.py executes inside Blender's own bundled interpreter, where neither pydantic nor this project's modules are importable.

manifest_version.description: Contract version. Consumers must reject a major version they do not know. Additive optional fields keep the version; removing or repurposing a field requires a bump. 1.1 added label_content.active_ingredient_display as REQUIRED, which is deliberately not an additive-optional change: a manifest written before it exists must fail validation and be regenerated rather than silently produce a packshot with a missing label row. 1.2 added carton.features and carton.material for the same reason - the side panel is drawn from them, and a stale manifest would render a panel missing its declared zones.

sku_id.description: Opaque SKU identifier, matching the passport's sku_id and keying into SSOT/SKU.csv. Never parse as a number.

template_id.description: Routing decision from agent_1_router(). Consumers must not re-derive this. Note T_VERT_* and T_BOTTLE_BOX denote the secondary CARTON for a vertical container, not the bottle or vial itself, so box geometry is correct for them.

is_bottle_override.description: Second half of the agent_1_router() decision: the SKU is physically a bottle or vial but is being placeholder-rendered as a generic carton. Reachable only through the geometry-family fallback and false for every SKU in the current catalogue; carried so the routing decision is represented in full rather than silently dropped.

packaging_geometry.description: Raw geometry class from the passport, retained so a renderer can branch on real form factor without reading the passport. Free-form rather than an enum because it is upstream source data; the values present today are BLISTER, BOTTLE, TUBE, PEN, VIAL, SACHET, BOX and INHALER.

carton.description: Dimensions of the SECONDARY packaging - the printed cardboard box that is actually rendered. This is deliberately NOT the primary package (the blister, bottle or syringe inside): the carton is the primary plus clearance, and for elongated primaries the axes are permuted, so the two are not interchangeable. Always present; when nothing better is known the template_ratio fallback still yields usable numbers, which is what frees consumers from null handling.

features.description: Construction features the carton declares, copied from the passport's secondary_packaging.features. Real per-SKU data, not decoration: 370 of the 391 cartons declare ["Braille", "DataMatrix_Zone", "Tamper_Evident_Seal"] and 21 declare nothing at all. A consumer draws a zone only when the carton claims it, instead of assuming every carton is identical.

material.description: Board specification from the passport's secondary_packaging.material, e.g. "GZ-Cardboard (Pharmaceutical Grade)". Printed on the side panel. It is real text the project already holds, which is the point: the reference renders fill that area with invented regulatory prose, and this engine prints only what it was given.

width_mm.description: Carton width in millimetres. Maps to the scene's X axis.

height_mm.description: Carton height in millimetres. Maps to the scene's Z axis (the box stands on the ground plane).

depth_mm.description: Carton depth in millimetres. Maps to the scene's Y axis.

source.description: Provenance of the three numbers above, so a consumer or a post-render check can tell measured data from a guess. passport_secondary: parsed straight from the passport's secondary_packaging.dimensions string, the most faithful path and the one taken by every SKU in the current catalogue. derived_from_primary: computed by resolve_secondary(get_primary_package(...)) when that string is missing or unparseable. template_ratio: no dimensional data at all, so the template's documented aspect ratio was applied to a nominal 100mm long edge.

palette.description: Brand colours. Note the surface-colour mandate: the carton body renders WHITE regardless of primary, and the brand colour appears only as the bottom accent stripe and the top-right badge. A consumer that paints the whole box in primary is not following the reference set.

label_content.description: Exact strings to render on the front face. A 3D renderer must reproduce these verbatim - the advantage over prompt-driven generation is precisely that the text cannot be hallucinated.

brand_name_display.description: Product name, top of the label grid. May wrap to two lines.

active_ingredient_display.description: Active ingredient, set regular weight on the row directly beneath the product name. Sourced from the passport's top-level active_ingredient, which is populated for all 391 SKU. It can be long - combination products reach 61 characters ("Sildenafil / Tadalafil / Vardenafil / Avanafil (Specimen Mix)") against a 30-character maximum for brand names - so a consumer must fit it to the face rather than assume it is short.

dosage_display.description: Dosage string such as "20mg", set bold at bottom-left. Contains at least one digit by Stage 1's verification rules.

unit_count_display.description: Quantity string such as "30 Pills", set regular at bottom-right.

hexColour.description: sRGB colour as an uppercase-or-lowercase six-digit hex triplet with a leading hash.
